subject: Engelska
title: Reading comprehension
sourceSummary: Short English texts where you practise finding information, understanding the main idea, drawing simple conclusions and guessing words from context.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

Tom is twelve years old and lives in Manchester. He goes to school by bus every morning. His favourite subject is history, but he thinks maths is difficult. After school he plays basketball with his friends.

How does Tom travel to school?
questions.opener: The answer is stated directly in the text. Look for the sentence about the journey to school.
questions.explanation: The second sentence says "He goes to school by bus every morning". Bike and car are not mentioned in the text at all — they are just distractors.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

Tom is twelve years old and lives in Manchester. He goes to school by bus every morning. His favourite subject is history, but he thinks maths is difficult. After school he plays basketball with his friends.

Which subject does Tom probably need the most help with?
questions.opener: The text does not say outright what he needs help with — but one word about a subject gives a clue.
questions.explanation: The text says he thinks maths is "difficult", so it is reasonable that he needs the most help there. History, on the contrary, is his favourite subject, so that answer does not fit.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

The school library is open from Monday to Friday. On weekdays it opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 4 p.m. It is closed on Saturdays and Sundays. Students can borrow up to five books at a time.

How many books can a student borrow at the same time?
questions.opener: Look for the number in the last sentence.
questions.explanation: The last sentence says "up to five books at a time", so at most five books. The number four comes from the opening time (4 p.m.) and has nothing to do with the number of books.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

The school library is open from Monday to Friday. On weekdays it opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 4 p.m. It is closed on Saturdays and Sundays. Students can borrow up to five books at a time.

Sara wants to visit the library on Sunday afternoon. What will happen?
questions.opener: Compare Sara's day with the days the text says the library is closed.
choices: The library will be open until 4 p.m.
questions.explanation: The text says the library is closed on Saturdays and Sundays, so Sara will arrive at a closed library. The times 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. only apply on weekdays.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

Many young people in Britain have a part-time job. Some of them deliver newspapers in the morning, and others work in a shop at the weekend. The money is useful, but it can be hard to do homework after a long day. Most students say it is important to find a good balance.

What is the main idea of the text?
questions.opener: The main idea concerns the whole text, not just a single sentence.
choices: Delivering newspapers is the best job for young people.
Young people in Britain should not work.
Part-time jobs give young people money but can make schoolwork harder.
Homework is more important than money.
questions.explanation: The text brings up both the advantage (the money is useful) and the disadvantage (it can be hard to do homework), which is the main idea. The claim that delivering newspapers would be the best job appears nowhere — it is only mentioned as an example.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

Many young people in Britain have a part-time job. Some of them deliver newspapers in the morning, and others work in a shop at the weekend. The money is useful, but it can be hard to do homework after a long day. Most students say it is important to find a good balance.

What does "deliver" mean in this text?
questions.opener: Think about what you do with newspapers in the morning — the context reveals the word.
questions.explanation: "Deliver newspapers" means to hand out newspapers to people's homes. The fact that it is about a morning job shows that it cannot mean "read" or "buy".

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer the two questions in full sentences.

Emma lives in a small town in Wales. She has two dogs and she walks them every afternoon. On Saturdays she helps her father in the garden, and in the evening she watches films with her mother.

1) How often does Emma walk her dogs?
2) What does Emma do on Saturday evenings?
questions.opener: Find the sentence that contains the key word in each question, and then answer with a full sentence.
questions.answer: 1) Emma walks her dogs every afternoon. 2) On Saturday evenings she watches films with her mother.
steps: Question 1 contains the key word "walk". Find the sentence with "walks them every afternoon" in the text.
Answer with a full sentence and replace "them" with what it refers to: "Emma walks her dogs every afternoon."
Question 2 contains the key word "evening". The text says "in the evening she watches films with her mother".
Check that the verb gets -s since "she" is third person singular: "she watches", not "she watch".

questions.prompt: How do you read an English text and answer the questions?
questions.opener: A four-step process — plus tricks for difficult words.
questions.answer: Step 1: read the whole text quickly to see what it is about · Step 2: read the question and look for the key word in the text — the answer to a fact question is almost always in the same sentence · Step 3: answer and check that you can point to the answer in the text. Main idea = what applies to the whole text, not a single example · an answer option that is only true for one sentence is usually wrong. Inference = combine what the text says with common sense · never make up facts that are missing. Difficult words: don't stop — read the sentence before and after and guess from the context. Common traps: options with words that appear in the text but answer the wrong question · numbers that belong to something else in the text. Answer in full sentences when the question asks for it, and replace pronouns like it and them with what they refer to.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

The Green Valley School has just built a new sports hall. It has a swimming pool, a climbing wall and three basketball courts. Students can use the sports hall every day after lessons, but they must book the climbing wall in advance because it is very popular.

What must students do before using the climbing wall?
questions.opener: The answer is stated directly in the text. Look for the sentence about the climbing wall.
choices: Ask a teacher for permission every time
questions.explanation: The text says students "must book the climbing wall in advance". A ticket and a helmet are never mentioned in the text.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

The Green Valley School has just built a new sports hall. It has a swimming pool, a climbing wall and three basketball courts. Students can use the sports hall every day after lessons, but they must book the climbing wall in advance because it is very popular.

Why do students probably need to book the climbing wall in advance?
questions.opener: The text gives you a clue in the very same sentence as the booking requirement.
choices: Because it is broken most days
Because it is only open on Fridays
Because teachers use it every day
questions.explanation: The text explicitly says "because it is very popular", which explains why booking is required. It being broken or only open on Fridays is never mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

Plastic pollution is a growing problem in the world's oceans. Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic end up in the sea, and much of it breaks into tiny pieces called microplastics. Fish and birds sometimes eat these pieces by mistake, which can make them ill. Many countries are now trying to use less plastic in shops and restaurants.

What is the main idea of the text?
questions.opener: The main idea is about the whole text, not just a single sentence.
choices: Fish always die from eating plastic
Plastic in the oceans is a serious problem that many countries are trying to reduce
questions.explanation: The text describes the problem (plastic in the oceans, microplastics, animals getting ill) and ends by saying countries are trying to reduce plastic use — that is the main idea. That fish always die or that restaurants should close is never stated.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

Plastic pollution is a growing problem in the world's oceans. Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic end up in the sea, and much of it breaks into tiny pieces called microplastics. Fish and birds sometimes eat these pieces by mistake, which can make them ill. Many countries are now trying to use less plastic in shops and restaurants.

What does "microplastics" mean in this text?
questions.opener: The word "micro" gives a clue about the size, and the sentence explains where the pieces come from.
choices: A machine that cleans the ocean
questions.explanation: The text says the plastic "breaks into tiny pieces called microplastics" — so they are small pieces of broken-down plastic. The word is not about a fish species or a country.

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

Oliver's family are going camping next weekend. They will drive to a campsite near a lake on Friday evening and stay until Sunday. Oliver is in charge of packing the tent, while his sister packs the food. On Saturday they plan to go fishing and swimming.

Who is packing the food for the camping trip?
questions.opener: The answer is stated directly in the text — look for the sentence about who packs what.
choices: Nobody, they will buy food there
questions.explanation: The text says "his sister packs the food". Oliver is instead in charge of the tent, according to the same sentence.

questions.prompt:
Read the text and answer the two questions in full sentences.

Oliver's family are going camping next weekend. They will drive to a campsite near a lake on Friday evening and stay until Sunday. Oliver is in charge of packing the tent, while his sister packs the food. On Saturday they plan to go fishing and swimming.

1) When will the family arrive at the campsite?
2) What are they planning to do on Saturday?
questions.opener: Find the sentence that contains the key word in each question, and then answer with a full sentence.
questions.answer: 1) The family will arrive at the campsite on Friday evening. 2) On Saturday they are planning to go fishing and swimming.
steps: Question 1 contains the key word "arrive". The text says they "drive to a campsite... on Friday evening".
Answer with a full sentence: "The family will arrive at the campsite on Friday evening."
Question 2 contains the key word "Saturday". The text says "On Saturday they plan to go fishing and swimming".
Rewrite it as a full sentence: "On Saturday they are planning to go fishing and swimming."

questions.prompt:
Read the text:

Oliver's family are going camping next weekend. They will drive to a campsite near a lake on Friday evening and stay until Sunday. Oliver is in charge of packing the tent, while his sister packs the food. On Saturday they plan to go fishing and swimming.

What can you tell about Oliver from the text?
questions.opener: The text doesn't say it in those exact words — but one detail shows he has a responsibility.
choices: He has some responsibility for the trip
He will stay home this weekend
questions.explanation: Oliver being "in charge of packing the tent" shows he has a responsibility for the trip. It is his sister, not Oliver, who packs the food, and nothing in the text suggests he dislikes camping or is staying home.
